Hi My teku (paired with geth on devnet-3) node also writes an error message related with feeRecipient (for ExecutableDataV1) ``` 2021-12-07 20:09:38.642 WARN - Failed to verify execution payload for block 0xb80e7d1a54b21975cf60917d0449b5208c094f2d7729dbca318ce7b11a4b4737 java.util.concurrent.CompletionException: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Invalid remote response: -32602: invalid argument 0: missing required field 'feeRecipient' for ExecutableDataV1 .... ``` (docker image: consensys/teku:develop) Similar logs on lighthouse client (docker image: sigp/lighthouse:latest-unstable) ``` WARN [12-07|20:18:21.453] Served engine_executePayloadV1 conn=127.0.0.1:51822 reqid=13 t="601.369µs" err="invalid argument 0: missing required field 'feeRecipient' for ExecutableDataV1" ``` If you are running the latest `:develop` (or master branch) of Teku then (aiui) you need to specify `--Xvalidators-suggested-fee-recipient-address <eth1 address>`. This was updated today to reflect the latest spec changes. previously i was using -Xvalidators-fee-recipient-address i tried to change it as -Xvalidators-suggested-fee-recipient-address but then received an error message let me try again (i'm using docker image btw) Pawan is working on a fix for lighthouse, we'll announce info soon 🙂 and ben's right, setting the new flag shouldn't give you that error on teku, i can share the image i'm using if it helps teku: `parithoshj/teku:merge-b6d8129` thanks, i was using consensys/teku:develop `consensys/teku:develop` should work but you need to make sure you have the latest version (`docker pull consensys/teku:develop`). https://storage.googleapis.com/mergedevnet-launchpad/index.html This now works apart from having to navigate to "Launchpad home". Was able to get 3 deposits in which were mined. Unfortunately can't see them on the explorers because of the network issues, but my balance was updated in metamask. I'm catching up on the fun of devnet-3 and not entirely sure what the actual canonical chain is. Current state from what I can see: - teku+nethermind remains broken because nethermind just keeps returning `SYNCING` forever (same problem we saw on devnet-2) - teku+geth can sync "a" chain and is producing blocks and attestations. - forkmon shows teku+geth to be insync with lighthouse+geth and nimbus+geth, nimbus+nethermind and lodestar+nethermind - block explorer seems to be following a different chain or just isn't syncing properly and isn't showing the teku+geth blocks. So I think I believe forkmon and teku+geth is doing ok (there were some failures to produce blocks earlier which I'll try to dig into). things should stabilize on devnet-3 now. - agreed, nethermind had an update for me that i'm yet to apply, unsure if its related - teku + geth seems to be on the right chain and doing things correctly now. unsure what changed compared to earlier when it failed to produce blocks. - forkmon might be outdated right now, it doesnt handle updates too well. a restart should fix it to show the correct info - block explorer should have caught up now - i've deployed pawan's lighthouse fix on the chain, so a ton of vals should be back up. for anyone else, use this branch for lighthouse: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/commits/merge-devnet-3 Closing the loop on the teku+geth block production failures - we were failing to produce the merge block itself. I've found one issue on the teku side but that wouldn't cause the failure we actually saw on the testnet so that needs some more work.

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content:
I'm catching up on the fun of devnet-3 and not entirely sure what the actual canonical chain is.  Current state from what I can see:
- teku+nethermind remains broken because nethermind just keeps returning `SYNCING` forever (same problem we saw on devnet-2)
- teku+geth can sync "a" chain and is producing blocks and attestations. 
- forkmon shows teku+geth to be insync with lighthouse+geth and nimbus+geth, nimbus+nethermind and lodestar+nethermind
- block explorer seems to be following a different chain or just isn't syncing properly and isn't showing the teku+geth blocks.

So I think I believe forkmon and teku+geth is doing ok (there were some failures to produce blocks earlier which I'll try to dig into).

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
things should stabilize on devnet-3 now. 

- agreed, nethermind had an update for me that i'm yet to apply, unsure if its related
- teku + geth seems to be on the right chain and doing things correctly now. unsure what changed compared to earlier when it failed to produce blocks.
- forkmon might be outdated right now, it doesnt handle updates too well. a restart should fix it to show the correct info 
- block explorer should have caught up now

- i've deployed pawan's lighthouse fix on the chain, so a ton of vals should be back up. for anyone else, use this branch for lighthouse: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/commits/merge-devnet-3

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Closing the loop on the teku+geth block production failures - we were failing to produce the merge block itself. I've found one issue on the teku side but that wouldn't cause the failure we actually saw on the testnet so that needs some more work.
